strings.name: Theaster Gates
strings.role: Artist · Ceramics, performance and community spaces
strings.summary: Gates combines ceramics, music, archives and building reuse to ask how objects, land and Black labor acquire value. Rebuild Foundation and Stony Island Arts Bank bring exhibitions, collections and community activity together on Chicago's South Side. He creates art while sustaining long-term cultural infrastructure; recent work continues his study of enslaved potter David Drake's legacy.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Combines ceramics, performance and community redevelopment through Chicago projects exploring art, urban renewal and Black cultural preservation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: East Garfield Park, Chicago, United States.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Iowa State bachelor's in 1996 and urban planning master's in 2006; also trained in pottery in Japan.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Art as cultural infrastructure
strings.highlights.h1.text: Rebuild and the Arts Bank reconnect abandoned spaces, archives and public activities.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Ceramics and historical inheritance
strings.highlights.h2.text: Links Japanese pottery training and David Drake research with making, labor and Black authorship.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Dave project exhibited in New York
strings.timeline.t1.text: Honored David Drake and commemorated gifting a historical vessel to his descendants.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Unto Thee opened in Chicago
strings.timeline.t2.text: The Smart Museum used discarded objects, archives and new works to trace his local relationships.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Black Chapel pavilion opened
strings.timeline.t3.text: Created a Serpentine space for gathering and music, extending research into materials, ritual and public life.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Arts Bank opened and Artes Mundi awarded
strings.timeline.t4.text: Stony Island Arts Bank became a cultural space; he shared the prize money with fellow shortlisted artists.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Participated in documenta 13
strings.timeline.t5.text: 12 Ballads for Huguenot House linked Kassel and Chicago through repair, exchanged materials and performance.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Founded Rebuild Foundation
strings.timeline.t6.text: Established a nonprofit platform using culture and art to regenerate community spaces.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Presented Plate Convergence
strings.timeline.t7.text: Used a fictional Japanese potter's story, ceramics and a communal meal to explore cultural exchange and social relationships.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed undergraduate studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Encountered ceramics and planning at Iowa State, laying foundations for later work across disciplines.
